name: Accessibility
first: What assistive technologies, such as VoiceOver, read and do for each view, which SwiftUI makes from the views themselves, and which modifiers can change.

dependsOn.why: A view's accessibility is changed with modifiers.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The call `accessibilityLabel` is a modifier of the star, as `padding(8)` is a modifier of `city`.

dependsOn.why: An image of a symbol shows no words, so it needs a label for VoiceOver to read.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The image `Image(systemName: "star.fill")` shows a symbol, as `Image(systemName: "star")` does on the page of Image.

what.is: Accessibility is what assistive technologies, such as VoiceOver, which reads the screen aloud, read and do for each view. SwiftUI makes it from the views: a `Text` is read as its words, and a button is read as a button. Modifiers change it, such as `accessibilityLabel`, which says what VoiceOver reads, and `accessibilityAddTraits`, which says what kind of thing a view is.
what.afterExample: VoiceOver would read the star as Favorite, a button, in place of the symbol's name, and the number 3 as 3 nights. A program with no screen reader prints the types: the image with a modifier that holds its accessibility, and a `Text`, whose label stays part of the text.
what.problem: Many people use an iPhone without seeing the screen, or with larger text, or with a switch in place of touch. A symbol or a number alone can mean nothing when it is read aloud. Accessibility gives each view words and a kind, so that everyone can use the app.
what.how: SwiftUI builds the accessibility of each view from what the view is: the words of a `Text`, the title of a button, and that a toggle is on or off. Apple's documentation says to give a label to a view that shows no text, such as an icon, and not to repeat in the label what a trait already says, such as the word button.

when.text: Use a label for every view that shows no words, such as a symbol, and for words that mean little alone, such as a number without its unit.
Don't label a view whose words already say what it is, such as a `Text` of a city. SwiftUI already reads it, and a label that repeats it says it twice.
